entries.title: II Corinthians 10:1
segments: Lowly among you. Paul was slow to assume a lordship over the Corinthians (
) even to the extent of administering a rebuke in person.  See

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:2
segments: Bold against some. Paul had personal enemies in the church at Corinth who found fault with his conduct (
) and with his teachings.  Against these he would be bold.  See also

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:5
segments: Exalted against the knowledge of God. The chief scourge of the early Christian church was the body of false teachers who sprang up and deceived many by their worldly interpretations of the gospel.  See

.
 

 
 Into captivity to the obedience of Christ. The false teachers seized upon Christianity as an excuse to escape obedience as to the law, and claimed freedom from sin through the sacrifice of Christ, while still remaining in unrighteousness.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:7
segments: Ye look at the things that are before your face.   According to outward appearance.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:8
segments: Our authority. Paul's mission to the Gentiles rested upon a special divine appointment.  See

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:12
segments: Comparing themselves with themselves. The value of a comparison depends upon the standard.  Paul measures himself by the magnitude of the work entrusted to him.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:13
segments: To reach even unto you. The gospel was given primarily to the Jews only.  Through the commissioning of Paul it was extended even unto the Gentiles; that is, to the whole world.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:15
segments: Not glorying... in other men's labors.  The inference here is that Paul's opponents had seized upon the organized church at Corinth, the fruit of Paul's labors, as a ready made field for their 'imaginations' (
). Paul suggests that there is abundant territory still untouched in 'the parts beyond you.' See
